newsitem.title: UK: FX IN EUROPE - MARK JUMPS HIGHER AFTER BUBA REPORT.
newsitem.headline: FX IN EUROPE - MARK JUMPS HIGHER AFTER BUBA REPORT.

text.p: The mark hogged the limelight on Wednesday, rising across the board in the wake of a hawkish assessment on German inflation by the Bundesbank.

The German unit rose to its highest level against the dollar in almost two weeks after the Bundesbank said in its August monthly report inflation had picked up and that it would steer policy to ensure price stability is maintained.
"The Bundesbank's more hawkish tone increased speculation about a rise in German rates and helped boost the mark," said James McKay, international economist at Paine Webber.
Dollar/mark fell about three pfennigs in European trading, while the mark rose to a six-week peak against sterling and to its highest since late June against the peseta.
Sterling tumbled below 2.90 marks - almost five pfennigs during the European session - as the mark muscled higher. It held fairly steady against the dollar though.

The pound was also weighed down by indications from the Bank of England in its quarterly inflation report that interest rates are now likely to be on hold, traders said. Better-than-expected July unemployment data and flat average earnings in June had little net impact.
A report in a London newspaper - saying Germany and France have hinted they would pe prepared to delay the start of EMU if the UK will join the first wave added some pressure, traders said.
But a German government spokesman dismissed the report as "pure speculation" and a British Treasury official declined comment.

"Nobody gave that much credit to the report but it weighed on an already weak (UK) currency," said a senior trader at a German bank. "The main push lower came from the rise of the mark across the board though."
At 1550 GMT the dollar was at 1.8336/46 marks, down from 1.8638/48 in late Europe on Tuesday. Against the yen it was at 115.58/68 from 115.95/116.00.
Sterling/mark was at 2.8958/68, down from 2.9399/9404 in late Europe on Tuesday. Cable was at $1.5818/28 from $1.5770/80.
Forex traders took the Bundesbank's hawkish tone on inflation as an indication that the central bank might be preparing the ground for higher German rates.

McKay at Paine Webber said he was sceptical though that a German rate rise was imminent. "Typically you don't see higher import prices because of the weaker currency feed through into consumer prices," he said. "It remains to be seen if the weak mark is going to push up consumer price inflation in Germany."

Economists said today's flurry of mark buying was not the start of a new trend. "The reasons why the mark fell so much before are still in place, such as the expectation that EMU will start on time with a broad base of members," said Mark Geddes, treasury economist at ABN AMRO.
The dollar got a small boost from U.S. data showing a monthly rise of 0.6 percent in retail sales in July and a drop of 0.1 percent in producer prices in the same month.

The dollar's weakness depressed dollar/yen even though general yen sentiment remains on the soft side given the state of the Japanese economy, dealers said. A recommendation from the International Monetary Fund that Japan should raise rates later in the year hurt dollar/yen in late trade here.
Mark/yen pushed above 63 yen and was at 63.02/05 in late Europe from 62.24.27 at the Tuesday close.

Dealers cited talk the Norwegian central bank, intervened to steady the crown. The currency had been volatile recently. The crown had risen to a three-month peak of 4.1180 against the mark on Monday as it drew some strength from firmer oil prices. On Wednesday it was at its lowest in almost a month at t 4.1460/90 in late trade from 4.1080/1100 at the previous close.
